ai.title: New integrations package for third-party services
ai.summary: Added `@codebuff/integrations` package to centralize third-party service logic. Migrated Loops email utility from `backend/src/util/loops.ts` to `packages/integrations/src/loops/`, replacing raw fetch calls with the official `loops` SDK client. Updated `evals` and `web` auth/invite routes to consume the new package. Consolidated fileChangeHooks in `codebuff.json` by merging typecheck commands into unit test hooks.

eli5.text: The system now routes all its emails through a single, well-maintained email service connection, instead of each part of the app building its own. This means email-sending from both the evaluation results and the web signup flow now share one reliable method that handles errors and logs failures properly behind the scenes. You won’t notice a visual difference, but emails like invite links and eval summaries are now less likely to silently break if the service misbehaves. The change is live today for anyone receiving an invite or an eval email.

ai.title: Add e2e cat app test script
ai.summary: Added `e2e-cat-app-script.ts` to `evals` to run end-to-end tests against a 'cat app' backend and CLI. Includes `test:e2e-cat-app` npm script in `evals/package.json`.

eli5.text: A new automated test script was added to the project's evaluation suite to verify the end-to-end functionality of a sample "cat app" backend and command-line interface. This test can be run using the npm script test:e2e-cat-app and will start the backend, interact with the CLI, and validate expected behaviors within configurable timeouts. It affects developers or CI systems that run the evals suite by adding a new validation path for the cat app integration, ensuring it works as expected from a clean state. If you looked at the project, you'd see a new test file e2e-cat-app-script.ts and a corresponding entry in package.json, with no impact on production user-facing features today.

ai.title: Add error logging to validateAutoTopupStatus
ai.summary: Added `logger.error` call in `validateAutoTopupStatus` catch block in `packages/billing/src/auto-topup.ts`. Ensures auto-topup validation failures are logged with error context. Internal change only, no user-facing behavior impact.

eli5.text: If the system runs into a problem while checking your auto-topup settings, it now makes a note of what went wrong and logs the details, instead of quietly failing. This is a behind-the-scenes change to help the team investigate rare errors more easily. No one sees a difference in how the feature works, and it is already live.

ai.title: Resolve invitation first name from DB instead of request payload
ai.summary: sendOrganizationInvitationEmail in packages/integrations/src/loops/client.ts now queries the user table via Drizzle to fetch the recipient's name, splitting the full name to extract the first token. The LoopsEmailData interface in types.ts drops the optional firstName field, making organizationName and inviterName required. Callers in web/src/app/api/orgs/[orgId]/invitations/route.ts and bulk/route.ts no longer pass firstName, relying on the integration to resolve it or default to 'there' if the user record is missing or lookup fails.

eli5.text: When someone is invited to join an organization, the email they receive will now greet them by their first name taken directly from their existing user profile in the system, rather than relying on the name provided in the invitation request. If no user profile exists for the invited email address, the email will default to a generic greeting like 'Hi there'. This change makes the invitation emails more accurate and prevents situations where an incorrect or missing name in the request could lead to a mismatched greeting.

ai.title: Team invite fixes
ai.summary: Consolidated invitation API routes into a single dynamic handler and bulk route. Switched invitation URL generation to use env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL instead of request.nextUrl.origin. Updated team management UI and invite page to match new API structure.

eli5.text: The system that sends and manages team invitations has been cleaned up so that adding, resending, and removing people from a group now goes through a single, more organized set of pathways instead of several separate ones. As a result, invitation links sent by email now always point to the correct company web address, even when the request comes from a background job or a different internal service, so people who click the link land on the right page without errors. If you invite someone to a group today, the invite page and the team settings screen you interact with have been updated to match, so the experience is more consistent and less likely to break. The change is live now for all organizations using the team management features.

ai.title: Remove old planning doc
ai.summary: Deleted `codebuff-export-agent-mode-planning.md`. This 140-line internal design document for Agent Mode is no longer relevant. Scope limited to repository root.

eli5.text: The team deleted an old internal planning document that described how they were thinking about building a new way for the assistant to handle multi-step coding tasks. It was a 140-line file sitting in the project's main folder, and nobody was using it anymore to guide development. If you opened the project today, you just wouldn't see that document there. It was housekeeping, not something that changed how the software works.

ai.title: Fix invite page layout and team management dialogs
ai.summary: Adjusted invite page container height and padding in web/src/app/invites/[token]/page.tsx by removing min-h-screen. Updated web/src/components/organization/team-management.tsx to replace native confirm dialogs with state-driven modal logic for invitation cancellation. Added confirmCancelDialogOpen state and removed unused handleRefresh function. These changes improve UI consistency and dialog handling in the organization management interface.

eli5.text: When you open an invitation email and click through to accept a team invite, the page no longer forces the content to stretch to the very bottom of your screen, so it looks properly centered with correct spacing around it. If your admin cancels a pending invitation while you're viewing the team management screen, you'll now see a built-in confirmation dialog instead of the browser's standard pop-up, making the experience feel smoother and more polished.

ai.title: Add @codebuff/integrations dep to evals
ai.summary: Added @codebuff/integrations as workspace dependency in evals/package.json. Fixes broken codebuff integrations within the evaluation suite. Scope limited to evals package dependencies.

eli5.text: The team that runs the automated tests for the assistant made a small edit to tell those tests where to find the codebuff integrations package. Previously the tests couldn't reach the integrations used to connect to third-party services, so things that depended on them failed silently; now the test setup points to the right place and the integrations work inside the test suite. This is a behind-the-scenes housekeeping change that fixes broken test coverage, and you wouldn't notice anything different in the product itself since it only affects how the internal tests are wired together.

ai.title: evals tsconfig adds integrations path reference
ai.summary: evals/tsconfig.json now maps `@codebuff/integrations/*` to `../packages/integrations/src/*` and adds a project reference to `../packages/integrations`. This enables the evals package to resolve types and imports from the integrations package during compilation. Change scoped to evals build configuration.

eli5.text: The system now lets the evaluation tools talk directly to the new integrations package so they can check that third-party service connections work, without needing to look elsewhere for the right code. This only affects the internal build setup, so you as a user won't see any difference, but behind the scenes it makes the testing process slightly smoother.

ai.title: Add evals project reference to tsconfig
ai.summary: Added `evals` to `tsconfig.json` project references. Enables TypeScript to resolve imports within the `evals` directory during builds. Scope limited to repo root `tsconfig.json`.

eli5.text: The TypeScript project's build configuration now includes the 'evals' directory as a recognized project reference, allowing the codebase to properly compile and link code from that evaluation tools folder. This change only affects internal development builds, no one outside the development team would notice any difference in the product itself. It is a behind-the-scenes adjustment that ensures the project builds correctly when evaluation code is present, but nothing observable changes for end users.

ai.title: evals: Add build script and fix promptAiSdkStructured call signature
ai.summary: Added `build` script (`tsc`) to `evals/package.json`. Updated `promptAiSdkStructured` calls in `evals/git-evals/` to use a single object argument with `messages` key instead of separate arguments, fixing type errors. This aligns with the expected function signature for structured prompting.

eli5.text: If you ran the internal evaluation scripts that test how well our AI models answer questions, those scripts would fail to even start or finish because of a small mismatch in how they were calling the model-under-test. The team corrected that calling convention across the evaluation scripts and added a build step so the scripts can compile properly before running. You wouldn't see this directly unless you were running the evaluation tooling, but it unblocks engineers who depend on those automated checks to validate model improvements.

ai.title: Terminal module split into base and background files
ai.summary: Refactored `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts` into `npm-app/src/terminal/base.ts` and `npm-app/src/terminal/background.ts`. This separates foreground terminal execution logic from background process management. Added `suffixPrefixOverlap` utility to `common/src/util/string.ts` for optimized string concatenation. All imports in `cli.ts`, `client.ts`, `dev-process-manager.ts`, `index.ts`, `json-config/hooks.ts`, and `tool-handlers.ts` updated to reflect new paths.

eli5.text: When the tool runs commands, it now splits the work into two cleaner jobs: one for commands that run in the open (like typing into a shell) and one for commands that run quietly in the background while you wait. This means background processes are no longer kept alive by accident after the assistant finishes with them, so they clean up properly instead of lingering. You won't notice a visual change, but behind the scenes the terminal handling is organized into two focused sections (foreground and background) instead of one crowded file, and a small helper was added that prevents duplicated text when stitching output together.

ai.title: Integrate evals into nx build system with dist output
ai.summary: evals package now compiles to dist/ via tsc, with scripts updated to reference compiled JS. New evals/project.json defines nx build, run-eval-set, and clean targets with dist output caching. Root package.json switches from explicit project list to nx run-many --all for build, clean, and typecheck-only. tsconfig.json adds outDir ./dist, rootDir ., and include **/*.ts.

eli5.text: The evals tooling now compiles to a shared output folder and the root build command runs across all projects automatically instead of listing each one. If you watched the repo, you'd see build errors vanish for eval scripts because they now run from compiled files, and a new configuration file in the evals folder declares how builds, eval runs, and cleanup steps work. It's live today and affects anyone running evals or full-repo builds.

ai.title: Update terminal import path in evals test-setup
ai.summary: Updated import in `evals/test-setup.ts` to source `recreateShell` from `npm-app/terminal/base` instead of `npm-app/utils/terminal`. This aligns the evals test setup with the current terminal module structure. Scope limited to internal test configuration.

eli5.text: The team adjusted a behind-the-scenes testing setup so that the automated checks used to evaluate the assistant's terminal behavior now connect to the terminal tool in its current home. This is internal configuration work that affects how the company's own quality tests run, not anything you'd see or change as a user. It's a small fix (one line) and is already in place, keeping the test suite consistent with the latest internal tool structure.

ai.title: Fix import path for terminal/base in git evals
ai.summary: Corrected import path for `recreateShell` in `evals/git-evals/run-git-evals.ts` to point to `npm-app/terminal/base`. Reordered imports to group external modules before internal ones and cleaned up trailing whitespace. This ensures the git evaluation runner resolves the terminal utility correctly.

eli5.text: You won't notice anything different here - this is behind-the-scenes cleanup. The engineering team fixed how their internal testing tool finds the right terminal program when running git evaluations, making sure it looks in the correct location. They also tidied up the order of some commands and removed extra spaces, which keeps the codebase organized and easier to maintain.

ai.title: Evals build depends on clean target
ai.summary: evals/project.json build target now depends on 'clean' alongside '^build'. This ensures dist is cleared before compilation. Scope limited to Evals package configuration.

eli5.text: When the automated evaluation tests run, the system now automatically clears out old built files before compiling new ones. This only affects the internal evaluation package used by developers to test AI model responses. The change is already live today and you wouldn't notice anything different in your daily work, but evaluations will now start from a clean state instead of potentially mixing old and new test outputs.

ai.title: gemini-2.5-pro-preview-06-05 replaces 05-06 in constants
ai.summary: The `gemini2_5_pro_preview` model identifier in `common/src/constants.ts` updated from `gemini-2.5-pro-preview-05-06` to `gemini-2.5-pro-preview-06-05`. This aligns the core constants with the latest Gemini Pro release. The change affects the shared model registry used across all Freebuff surfaces.

eli5.text: The assistant that powers the product quietly started using Google's newest Gemini Pro model version, dated June 5 instead of May 6. This swap happened in a shared settings file so every part of the service now references the updated model automatically. If you interacted with the assistant after this change went live, your conversation was processed by this newer version without any action required on your end.

ai.title: Add codebuff workspace dependency to evals
ai.summary: Added `codebuff` to `dependencies` in `evals/package.json` and `implicitDependencies` in `evals/project.json`. This establishes an explicit workspace link to the core `codebuff` package for the evaluation suite. Scope limited to `evals` project configuration files. Dependency uses `workspace:*` protocol to ensure local package resolution.

eli5.text: The team behind the assistant’s test setup added a direct link to the assistant’s own core software inside the internal test tool. This only touches the testing environment that staff use to check how the assistant behaves; it doesn’t change what you see today. If you looked behind the scenes you’d see the test system now pulls the same assistant code used everywhere else, so tests stay in sync as that core software changes. Live today for anyone running those internal evaluations.

ai.title: Remove gemini-2.5-pro-exp-03-25 model references
ai.summary: Removed gemini2_5_pro_exp and its OpenRouter alias from common/src/constants.ts. Updated scripts/ft-file-selection/relabel-traces.ts to cast model as gemini2_5_pro_preview. Covers core model registry and internal trace tooling. Existing references to the deprecated experimental model are now stripped from type definitions and provider mappings.

eli5.text: The assistant has retired an experimental version of one of its AI models and is now pointing everyone to the newer, official version of that same model instead. If you were watching system logs or internal tracing tools, you might have noticed that references to the old experimental model are gone and replaced with the stable one. This affects only the internal systems that select and label which model handles requests, so everyday users won't see a difference in how things work, but the software is now working with a single, consistent model rather than switching between an old experimental one and the newer release.

ai.title: Fix terminal command hangs and split hooks
ai.summary: Terminal commands no longer hang due to incorrect output parsing in `npm-app/src/terminal/base.ts`. The `commandDonePattern` regex now uses `cwdIdentifier` instead of `promptIdentifier` to correctly detect command completion. `codebuff.json` file change hooks are split: unit tests and typechecks run as separate hooks for backend, npm-app, web, and common, replacing the chained `&&` commands.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to run a terminal command (like a shell instruction in the dev environment), it would sometimes freeze and never finish, the tool would get stuck waiting for the command to complete. Now the tool correctly detects when each command is actually done, so commands finish properly instead of hanging forever. This mainly affects developers using the internal tooling, not end users.

ai.title: Add @homebridge/node-pty-prebuilt-multiarch to evals
ai.summary: Added @homebridge/node-pty-prebuilt-multiarch (0.12.0-beta.5) to evals/package.json dependencies. Fixes homebridge installation in evals. Affects evals package only.

eli5.text: The automated testing suite used to check the assistant's work can now install and run Homebridge, a tool for connecting smart home devices, during its evaluations. This only affects the internal testing environment, not any live features you use. If you were to look at the testing setup, you would find Homebridge installation succeeding where it previously failed. This fix is live today for anyone running the test suite.

ai.title: Remove terminal cwdIdentifier tracking and consolidate hooks
ai.summary: Removed `cwdIdentifier` logic from `npm-app/src/terminal/base.ts` and deleted `runSinglePtyCommand`. `codebuff.json` hooks now merge unit tests and typechecks, using ANSI-stripping regex for cleaner output.

eli5.text: The internal development tools that automatically check your code for mistakes when you save were simplified. Instead of watching each part of your project in separate steps, the tool now runs all the checks together and shows cleaner results without color codes. This means when you save a file, the background checks that make sure nothing broke will run faster as one combined check rather than a few separate ones. Nothing about how you use the software changed, but this makes the behind-the-scenes process that keeps things running smoothly a bit more efficient.

ai.title: Exclude dist from evals tsconfig
ai.summary: Added 'dist' to the exclude array in evals/tsconfig.json. This prevents TypeScript from attempting to compile or type-check generated artifacts within the evals directory. Scope is limited to the evals subsystem configuration.

eli5.text: This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping for the internal testing tools: the team updated the configuration that governs how the testing system checks the evaluation code, adding a "dist" folder to the list of items it should ignore. Only engineers running the evaluation tests are affected; they will notice the testing tools skip a generated output folder that they previously tried to process and flag errors on. No customer-facing change.

ai.title: Drop evals build step
ai.summary: Removed `build` script and `outDir` from `evals/package.json` and `evals/tsconfig.json`. Eval scripts now run TypeScript files directly via `bun run` instead of compiled JS in `dist/`. File `run-eval-set.ts` moved to `git-evals/` directory, updating relative imports. No user-facing changes.

eli5.text: The team removed the step that converted their testing scripts into a different format before running them, so those scripts now run directly instead. If you looked behind the scenes, you would notice there is no longer a folder that held the converted versions of those scripts, and the helper files used by the main script were moved into a subfolder. This only affects people working directly on the testing tools and does not change anything you see.

ai.title: Remove evals build target and IPty type
ai.summary: Removed build, clean, and dependsOn targets from evals/project.json. run-eval-set now executes git-evals/run-eval-set.ts directly via bun. Replaced specific IPty type with any in npm-app/src/terminal/base.ts PersistentProcess union. Dropped @homebridge/node-pty-prebuilt-multiarch type import.

eli5.text: The internal evaluation tooling that checks how the assistant behaves on certain prompts no longer needs a separate build step before it runs; it now starts straight from its original source files using the Bun runtime, so whoever triggers an evaluation set sees it begin immediately instead of waiting for a compile step first. The terminal session manager inside the app also stopped relying on a strict third-party type definition for its pseudo-terminal handle, so it now treats that handle as a generic value, which prevents type mismatches from blocking the build when the optional terminal backend package isn't installed. These are backstage adjustments for the team that runs assistant evaluations and for the app's interactive terminal feature; both areas were live today once a developer
